correctness.rationale: With full power spectrum, odd-frequency ratios h have modulus one and conjugation. The m trispectral equations force \(h(2j+1)=h(1)^{2j+1}\); both N mod 4 cases imply \(h(1)^N=1\). Thus ratios are precisely character phases of translations. Fewer than m individual trispectrum coordinates define at most s torus characters on the m-dimensional fixed-magnitude phase torus and leave a positive-dimensional nontranslation ambiguity. Verified directly and algebraically by CHECK.py (1011107 assertions), without treating finite computation as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The full odd-frequency support class is a natural exact Fourier-zero obstruction to bispectral inversion: all odd-order autocorrelations vanish. An explicit reconstruction algorithm using exactly m entries and a matching nonadaptive information lower bound specifies the minimal fourth-order data needed to overcome this obstruction. This is a meaningful sharp sampling design and universal classification of the measurement threshold, not a small numerical gain.
